```{python}
#| output: false
import numpy as np
import polars as pl
from pathlib import Path
from plotnine import (
    ggplot, aes, geom_point, geom_histogram, geom_boxplot, geom_abline,
    labs, theme_minimal, facet_wrap,
)
from great_tables import GT
from IPython.display import HTML, display

ROOT = Path.cwd()
while not (ROOT / "mlb" / "fielding_models" / "parquet").is_dir():
    ROOT = ROOT.parent
FM = ROOT / "mlb" / "fielding_models" / "parquet"

def fam(stem):
    fs = sorted(FM.glob(f"{stem}_*.parquet"))
    frames = []
    for f in fs:
        d = pl.read_parquet(f)
        if "season" not in d.columns:
            d = d.with_columns(pl.lit(int(f.stem.rsplit("_", 1)[-1])).alias("season"))
        frames.append(d)
    return pl.concat(frames, how="diagonal_relaxed")

oaa = fam("mlb_oaa")
frm = fam("mlb_catcher_framing")
SEASONS = sorted(oaa["season"].unique().to_list())

def gt_show(g):
    display(HTML(g.as_raw_html()))

def mlbam_names(ids):
    ids = [int(i) for i in ids]
    try:
        import requests
        out = {}
        for i in range(0, len(ids), 80):
            chunk = ids[i:i + 80]
            r = requests.get("https://statsapi.mlb.com/api/v1/people",
                             params={"personIds": ",".join(map(str, chunk))}, timeout=20)
            for p in r.json().get("people", []):
                out[int(p["id"])] = p.get("fullName", str(p["id"]))
        return {i: out.get(i, str(i)) for i in ids}
    except Exception:
        return {i: str(i) for i in ids}
```

Two surfaces ship on the `mlb_fielding_models` release tag: **Outs Above
Average** over balls in play, and **catcher framing** (called-strike value
above average at the zone edges). The builders live in sdv-py
(`mlb_fielding_oaa`, `mlb_catcher_framing`) over Baseball Savant balls-in-play
and pitch-location data; this repository commits per-season outputs under
`mlb/fielding_models/` and publishes them daily in-season.

The design constraint is stated up front because it prices the gates: the
public feed lacks fielder start coordinates, so OAA here conditions on
batted-ball properties and fielder identity rather than true opportunity
geometry — a **feature-capped ceiling that is priced into the gates** (OAA
full-season Pearson vs Savant's live OAA ≥ 0.55; framing ≥ 0.40) instead of
hidden. The registry also records what is deliberately NOT published from
this family (catcher throwing/blocking, baserunning, SB value): their live
floors of 0.03–0.073 against 0.80+ design targets are data-ceiling-limited,
recorded so nobody "finds" the gap later.

Given that ceiling, the evaluation that matters most is **year-over-year
reliability** — whether the surviving metrics measure something stable about
the fielder rather than re-rolling noise annually. That is computed below
across every adjacent committed season pair, per position for OAA.

## Training data

```{python}
tbl = (
    oaa.group_by("season").agg(pl.len().alias("fielders"),
                               pl.col("opportunities").sum().alias("opportunities"))
    .join(frm.group_by("season").agg(pl.len().alias("catchers"),
                                     pl.col("takes").sum().alias("takes")),
          on="season", how="full", coalesce=True)
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(tbl.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Committed fielding-model assets, by season",
                subtitle="from mlb/fielding_models/parquet/; computed at render time")
    .fmt_number(columns=["opportunities", "takes"], sep_mark=",", decimals=0)
)
```

## Exploratory data analysis

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "OAA distribution by position, latest season."
latest = SEASONS[-1]
ol = oaa.filter(pl.col("season") == latest)
(
    ggplot(ol.to_pandas(), aes("position", "oaa"))
    + geom_boxplot(fill="#2a6f97", alpha=0.6)
    + labs(x="position", y="OAA", title=f"Outs Above Average by position — {latest}")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Framing runs vs strikes gained — the run value is a near-linear function of strikes."
(
    ggplot(frm.to_pandas(), aes("strikes_gained", "framing_runs"))
    + geom_point(alpha=0.4, color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="strikes gained", y="framing runs",
           title="Catcher framing — all committed seasons")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

The internal consistency check is visible in the framing scatter: framing
runs scale linearly with strikes gained at roughly the canonical run value of
a called strike. OAA centers near zero by construction at every position —
it is an *above-average* metric, so the league sums to ~0 each season:

```{python}
zero = (
    oaa.group_by(["season"]).agg(pl.col("oaa").sum().alias("league_oaa_sum"),
                                 pl.len().alias("fielders"))
    .sort("season")
)
gt_show(
    GT(zero.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="League OAA sum by season (zero-centering check)")
    .fmt_number(columns="league_oaa_sum", decimals=1)
)
```

## Evaluation — year-over-year reliability

```{python}
def yoy(df, key, col, extra=None):
    a = df.select([key, "season", pl.col(col).alias("v0")] + (extra or []))
    b = df.select(key, (pl.col("season") - 1).alias("season"), pl.col(col).alias("v1"))
    return a.join(b, on=[key, "season"], how="inner")

rows = []
for pos in sorted(oaa["position"].unique().to_list()):
    sub = oaa.filter(pl.col("position") == pos)
    j = yoy(sub, "fielder_id", "oaa")
    if j.height >= 30:
        rows.append({"metric": f"OAA — {pos}", "pairs": j.height,
                     "yoy_pearson": float(j.select(pl.corr("v0", "v1")).item())})
jf = yoy(frm, "catcher_id", "framing_runs")
rows.append({"metric": "Framing runs", "pairs": jf.height,
             "yoy_pearson": float(jf.select(pl.corr("v0", "v1")).item())})
rel = pl.DataFrame(rows).sort("yoy_pearson", descending=True)
gt_show(
    GT(rel.to_pandas())
    .tab_header(title="Year-over-year reliability — same fielder, adjacent seasons",
                subtitle="all committed season pairs pooled; higher = more stable skill")
    .fmt_number(columns="yoy_pearson", decimals=3)
)
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Framing runs, season S vs season S+1 — the most reliable fielding skill."
(
    ggplot(jf.to_pandas(), aes("v0", "v1"))
    + geom_abline(slope=1, intercept=0, linetype="dashed", color="gray")
    + geom_point(alpha=0.5, color="#2a6f97")
    + labs(x="framing runs (season S)", y="framing runs (season S+1)",
           title="Catcher framing YoY stability")
    + theme_minimal()
)
```

Framing is famously the stickiest defensive skill and the reliability table
reproduces that: catcher framing tops the list, while OAA reliability varies
by position with the infield generally steadier than the outfield at these
sample sizes. This is the correct lens for a feature-capped model — even
without start coordinates, a metric that correlates season-over-season is
measuring the fielder, not the noise.

topf = frm.filter(pl.col("season") == latest).sort("framing_runs", descending=True).head(10)

    pl.col("catcher_id").map_elements(lambda i: names[int(i)], return_dtype=pl.Utf8).alias("player"),

## Provenance & reproducibility

- **Trained on:** Baseball Savant balls-in-play (batted-ball properties +
  fielder identity; **no fielder start coordinates in the public feed**) and
  pitch locations for framing; seasons in the table above.
- **Committed at:** `mlb/fielding_models/parquet/`; published to
  `mlb_fielding_models`; per-publish metadata in
  [`../../mlb/fielding_models/mlb_fielding_models_card.json`](../../mlb/fielding_models/mlb_fielding_models_card.json).
- **Pipeline:** `scripts/mlb_models.sh 04` → stage
  `python/mlb_model_04_fielding.py` (`mlb_models_cron.yml`). Single home:
  `models/manifest.yaml`.
- **Rebuild this document:** `scripts/render_model_docs.sh` (Quarto → GFM;
  `uv sync --group docs`). Names/headshots via one batched statsapi call;
  offline renders fall back to MLBAM ids.

## Avenues for improvement & open issues

- **Start-coordinate ceiling** — the single biggest gain would be fielder
  positioning data, which the public feed does not carry; until then the
  gates stay at their priced-in floors (OAA ≥ 0.55, framing ≥ 0.40 vs live).
- **Publish per-direction OAA splits** — in/back/lateral splits exist in the
  substrate and would make the position-reliability differences diagnosable.
- **Known issue:** the registry's deliberately-unpublished surfaces (catcher
  throwing/blocking, baserunning, SB value) remain data-ceiling-limited
  (live floors 0.03–0.073 vs 0.80+ design targets) — recorded so the gap is
  never "discovered".
